construct: Activated factor XIII is a transglutaminase that covalently cross-links fibrin after fibrin formation, stabilizing the clot; factor XIII deficiency can cause significant delayed bleeding despite normal PT and aPTT because routine clotting times measure events before factor XIII-mediated cross-linking.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Delayed bleeding, umbilical-stump bleeding, and normal PT/aPTT point to factor XIII deficiency because factor XIII stabilizes already-formed fibrin by covalent cross-linking.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Intrinsic-tenase defects prolong aPTT; vitamin K pathway defects alter PT/aPTT; vWF disease is primarily an adhesion disorder; impaired thrombin-mediated fibrin formation would affect earlier clot formation rather than isolated post-formation stabilization.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The normal routine coagulation times are the decisive negative evidence: factor XIII acts downstream of the reactions measured by PT and aPTT.
